entries.name: Thames

facts.claim: Thames is an old gold-mining town on the west coast of the Coromandel Peninsula and the gateway to the peninsula; the Kauaeranga Valley hiking and camping area lies just south.
Thames is the seat of the Thames-Coromandel District Council and the largest town on the peninsula (Whitianga is second-largest).
Grahamstown, the northern end of Thames, has cafes and boutique shops, a museum covering Maori times, mining and logging, and a School of Mines open Wednesday to Saturday.

entries.name: Whitianga

facts.claim: Whitianga is a seaside town in the middle of Mercury Bay with a deep-water harbour from which cruising boats depart for the Mercury Bay coves and Te Whanganui-A-Hei Marine Reserve.
Whitianga has about 6,140 permanent residents (June 2025), the second-largest town on the peninsula behind Thames.
Cooks Beach is across the harbour from Whitianga, reached by a short passenger ferry.

entries.name: Kauaeranga Valley

facts.claim: DOC: the Kauaeranga Valley is in Coromandel Forest Park, 13 km behind Thames; it has campsites beside the Kauaeranga River and the Pinnacles (759 m) with panoramic views.

The Kauaeranga Visitor Centre (995C Kauaeranga Valley Road, Thames) has track, hut and campsite information and displays on kauri logging; the road is sealed to the visitor centre, then 9 km of gravel to the road end where most walks start.
A replica kauri-driving dam is a short walk from the visitor centre; Dancing Camp is the one logging dam still substantially intact.

entries.ticketUrl_note: Verified: DOC page (HTTP 200, title 'Kauaeranga Valley: Coromandel places to visit'). Replaces the placement's Coromandel Forest Park URL, which does not name the valley. Visitor centre hours are on a separate DOC page (not captured).

entries.name: Pinnacles Track

facts.claim: DOC's Kauaeranga Kauri Trail (Pinnacles Walk) is a popular 6 km one-way, about 3 hr walk from the Kauaeranga road end to Pinnacles Hut and on to the Pinnacles summit lookout (759 m); it can be a day or overnight walk.

Walk there and back on the Webb Creek Track takes 6 to 7 hr 30 min; the Webb Creek plus Billygoat circuit takes 7 to 8 hr 30 min. Pinnacles Hut to the summit is a further 40 min one way and more exposed.
The track starts at the road-end car park: cross the swing bridge over the Kauaeranga River, then take the Webb Creek Track to Hydro Camp.
Pinnacles Hut (80 bunks) must be booked online; DOC lists adult bunks at $30 to $40 a night depending on season (hut, not the day walk).

entries.ticketUrl_note: Verified: DOC page (HTTP 200, title 'Kauaeranga Kauri Trail: Coromandel Forest Park', heading 'Kauaeranga Kauri Trail (Pinnacles Walk)'). Replaces the placement's Pinnacles Hut page (hut booking page, not the track). Day walk is free; overnight hut is paid.

OSM node 330123959 'Billygoat Track Carpark' at -37.06842,175.66616 is ~0.8 km SW and is the Billygoat/Tarawaere Dam car park, not necessarily the road-end car park.

entries.name: Mount Pirongia

facts.claim: Mount Pirongia is an extinct stratovolcano rising to 959 m in the Waikato; Pirongia Forest Park is 25 km southeast of Hamilton.

DOC Tirohanga Track: 6.5 km, 3 to 5 hr one way, advanced tramping track from Corcoran Road car park over Ruapane Trig (723 m) to the Pirongia summit (959 m), with climbing chains on difficult parts; Taranaki and Ruapehu are visible on a clear day.
DOC: water is difficult to find on the high-level tracks, especially in summer, and many tracks are muddy after rain.

entries.ticketUrl_note: Verified: DOC park page (HTTP 200, title 'Pirongia Forest Park: Places to go in the Waikato region'). A track page (Tirohanga Track) also exists at the same site if a more specific link is wanted.

entries.name: Maungatautari

facts.claim: Sanctuary Mountain Maungatautari is New Zealand's largest pest-proof fenced eco-sanctuary around the extinct Maungatautari volcano near Cambridge; the visitor centre is at 99 Tari Road, Pukeatua, and the Southern Enclosure (Te Tui a Tane) is where passes and guided tours are sold.
Official hours: visitor centre 9am to 4pm daily, last entry 4pm, closed only on 25 December; day passes must be collected by 4pm.
Official experiences page: Day Pass into the Sanctuary from $34 per adult; guided tours from $50 to $72 per adult and include the pass.
No dogs, no bikes, and a biosecurity check/clean/close routine at the pest-proof gates; the site promotes kaka, takahe and tuatara.
Wikipedia: the 797 m mountain is an extinct stratovolcano and the site of the sanctuary.

entries.ticketUrl_note: Verified: official site (HTTP 200, titled 'Walking/Hiking Trails at Sanctuary Mountain Maungatautari' / 'Contact Us | Sanctuary Mountain Maungatautari').

coordinates_check.note: Pin at the visitor centre/entrance, not the summit.

unverified: Day Pass price is 'From $34' on the official page; third-party listings show $30 to $32 (older).
entries.bio_suggestion: A volcanic mountain fenced as a predator-free ecological island near Cambridge, where visitors can see native birds such as kaka and takahe.

entries.name: Timber Trail

facts.claim: DOC: the Timber Trail Pureora to Ongarue is an 85 km one-way, 2 to 3 day Grade 3 trail through Pureora Forest Park on old bush tramways, with 35 bridges including 8 large suspension bridges (longest 141 m) and the Ongarue Spiral; part of Te Araroa.
It begins on Barryville Road about 200 m from the DOC Pureora Field Base, across from the Timber Trail car park, and is reached off SH30 between Te Kuiti and Mangakino; most riders go north to south.
The DOC page lists no fee for the trail itself; the day-trip options include an 8 km Pureora Village to Pureora Maunga section and a 5 km crawler tractor loop.

entries.ticketUrl_note: Verified: DOC page (HTTP 200, title 'The Timber Trail - Pureora - Ongarue: Pureora Forest Park, Waikato region').

coordinates_check.source: OSM way 558279200 'Timber Trail', first node (shared with the Totara Walk), Barryville Road, Pureora (Nominatim lookup: first node -38.5136117, 175.5570114). OSM tags the area Waitomo District/Manawatu-Whanganui but DOC files it under Waikato. The earlier OSM point -38.5151,175.5695 is a mid-segment 1.3 km east.

unverified: Huts/campsites along the trail are paid separately (not researched).
entries.bio_suggestion: An 85 km, 2-3 day cycle and walking trail through Pureora Forest Park on a former logging tramway, from Pureora to Ongarue, with 35 bridges.

entries.name: Tirau Giant Dog and Sheep

facts.claim: Wikipedia: Tirau is characterised by corrugated-iron artworks; the information centre is shaped like a giant dog and the neighbouring building like a sheep, both completely made of corrugated iron.
Wikivoyage Matamata lists the giant dog and sheep metal structure at the Tirau visitor centre at -37.9769, 175.75632.
OSM: Tirau i-SITE Visitor Centre, Main Road (way 332808516) at -37.97691, 175.75640.

entries.name: Cathedral Cove

facts.claim: DOC's Mautohe Cathedral Cove Track: 5 km return, about 1 hr 30 min, easy to intermediate; starts at the top of Grange Road, Hahei (no parking there; Hahei Visitor Car Park has free parking and a shuttle runs to the entrance, 30 min walk otherwise) and ends at the rock archway at Mares Leg Cove.
DOC warns not to visit during or after heavy rain (high landslide risk); the track reopened 1 Dec 2024 and again on 31 Jan 2026 after a weather closure.
Wikipedia: 'Cathedral Cove' redirects to 'Whanganui A Hei (Cathedral Cove) Marine Reserve', whose article is about the marine reserve (840 ha), not the arch.

entries.ticketUrl_note: Verified: DOC page (HTTP 200, title 'Mautohe Cathedral Cove Track: Hahei area, Coromandel'). Currently no ticketUrl in spots.ts.

coordinates_check.source: OSM natural/bay node 1052610247 'Cathedral Cove'; beach way 90699216 at -36.8275,175.7894

unverified: Shuttle (Park & Ride) fare not captured; the walk is free.

entries.wiki_fix: Set `wiki: 'Whanganui A Hei (Cathedral Cove) Marine Reserve'` (the redirect target) to silence the lint, but that article is about the marine reserve, so check its lead photo shows the arch; otherwise keep the name and use a WIKI_IMAGE_OVERRIDES photo of the arch. entries.name: Hot Water Beach

facts.claim: Wikipedia (article title 'Hot Water Beach'): a beach on the east coast of the Coromandel Peninsula about 12 km southeast of Whitianga, where underground hot springs filter up through the sand between the tide lines; about 700,000 visitors a year.
Wikivoyage Hahei: the road to Hot Water Beach turns off the main road at Whenuakite.

entries.ticketUrl_note: Public beach; no single steward found (not DOC). Leave without ticketUrl.

coordinates_check.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Water_Beach (article point)
coordinates_check.note: ~950 m from the Wikipedia point; the current point is likely the south end/Hot Water Beach Road end where the springs are. Not changed; the beach is ~1 km long.

unverified: Best tide window (about two hours either side of low tide) not sourced here.
entries.wiki_fix: The lint is right: 'Hot Water Beach, New Zealand' has no article. The correct title is exactly 'Hot Water Beach' (it is the NZ beach; checked its summary). Change `wiki: 'Hot Water Beach, New Zealand'` to `wiki: 'Hot Water Beach'` or drop the field (name already matches).

entries.name: Marokopa Falls

facts.claim: DOC Marokopa Falls Walk: 600-700 m return, about 20 min, easy short walk to the 35 m high Marokopa Falls.
The falls are 31 km west of Waitomo on Te Anga Road with a small car park at the trailhead.
OSM has the waterfall node at -38.26164, 174.85196 and the viewpoint at -38.26132, 174.85071.

entries.ticketUrl_note: Verified: DOC page (HTTP 200, title 'Marokopa Falls Walk: Waitomo area, Waikato region'). Currently no ticketUrl in spots.ts.
